A Chinese scholar and official of the Song dynasty who wrote about almost everything: astronomy, mathematics, maps, medicine, geology and engineering. His Dream Pool Essays, written near the end of his life, are a key record of Song science.

He served under the reformer Wang Anshi, ran the court astronomy bureau, went as an envoy to the Liao in the north, and led troops on the western frontier. A defeat in 1082 ended his career, and he retired to a garden estate he called the Dream Pool.

In the Essays he:

  • gave the first clear description of a magnetic needle compass, and noted that it points not quite to true north;
  • recorded how the commoner Bi Sheng printed with movable clay type;
  • argued from fossil shells far inland that the land had once been under the sea and had been built up by silt over long ages.

Little of his work was taken further in China, but it is now one of the best windows on what Song thinkers knew.
